newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end sharply lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end sharply lower on consolidation.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended sharply lower on Thursday as investors took a breather and cashed their recent profits after the index moved into record-high territory for almost two weeks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index was down 8.99 points, or 1.22 percent, to close at 729.15 points after touching an intra-day low of 724.25 points.
Losers led gainers by 90 to 47, with 61 counters unchanged. Total volume was around 596 billion rupiah.
"I believe the market will remain at a consolidation stage on Friday," broker Suharto of Bhakti Investama said.
The stock market hit several record highs prior to the unveiling of the reform package, making widespread profit-taking inevitable, brokers said.

They said the sharp fall of the Dow Jones index overnight had triggered investors to cash out. Correction was seen mainly in Telkom, Semen Gresik, Indosat, Gudang Garam, and Bank International Indonesia.
Holding company Bakrie & Brothers, Bakrie Sumatra Plantations and Bakrieland Development were among favoured issues, brokers said.
Plantation firm Bakrie Sumatra had been actively traded since Monday on expectation of higher earnings after the government lowered the export tax structure on palm oil.
Brokers said strong sentiment on Bakrie Sumatra had improved sentiment on Bakrie Group-linked counters such as Bakrie & Brothers and Bakrieland Development.
Bakrie & Brothers topped the active list with about 63 million shares traded, rising 200 rupiah.
